'''''Prunus'' × ''subhirtella''''', the '''winter-flowering cherry''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=PRSU4|taxon=''Prunus subhirtella''|accessdate=15 October 2015}}</ref> '''spring cherry''', or '''rosebud cherry''',<ref>Bailey, L.H.; Bailey, E.Z.; the staff of the Liberty Hyde Bailey Hortorium. 1976. ''Hortus third: A concise dictionary of plants cultivated in the United States and Canada''. Macmillan, New York.</ref> is the scientific name for the hybrid between ''[[Prunus itosakura]]'' (edohigan) and ''[[Prunus incisa|Prunus incisa (Mamezakura)]]''.<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/94841/Prunus-x-subhirtella/Details | title = ''Prunus'' × ''subhirtella'' | publisher = RHS | access-date = 5 March 2021}}</ref><ref name ="grinito">[https://npgsweb.ars-grin.gov/gringlobal/taxon/taxonomydetail?id=480607 Taxon: ''Prunus itosakura'' Siebold.] GRIN-Global</ref><ref name ="katsuki201533">Toshio Katsuki. (2015) ''Sakura''. p.33. [[Iwanami Shoten]]. {{ISBN|978-4004315346}}</ref> It is a small [[deciduous]] flowering tree originating in [[Japan]], but unknown in the wild.
